chunks: When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed
"So glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most Great."
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Make it in your bowing."
Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed
"Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High."
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Make it in your prostration."

key_terms.رَبِّكَ: Your Lord, the One being glorified in worship.
key_terms.ٱجْعَلُوهَا: Make it part of your practice or recitation.
key_terms.ٱلْأَعْلَى: The Most High; linked here to sujud.
key_terms.ٱلْعَظِيمِ: The Most Great; linked here to ruku'.

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم apply the verses of tasbih to ruku' and sujud in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith links two Qur'anic commands of tasbih to specific positions in salat (prayer). The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed that glorification connected to "ٱلْعَظِيمِ" be recited in ruku' and that connected to "ٱلْأَعْلَى" be recited in sujud, showing how Qur'anic revelation informed prophetic prayer practice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.932 - When Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
"So glorify the name of your Lord (azj), the Most Great" (Surah Al-Waqi'ah, 56:74),
The Prophet (sw) said: "Make it a part of your bowing (ruku')."
Then, when Allah (swt), the Exalted, revealed:
"Glorify the name of your Lord (azj), the Most High" (Surah Al-A’lā, 87:1)
The Prophet (sw) said: "Make it a part of your prostration (Sujood)”.
